name: Michael Cremo
abstract_title: The boundary problem: a Vedic perspective
abstract: In light of the failure of any physicalist theory of consciousness to win general acceptance in the field of consciousness studies, some researchers are turning to theories that give consciousness its own independent status. This may take the form of panpsychism or cosmopsychism, in which consciousness is characterized as an all pervading monism. Others identify consciousness as a property of matter on the atomic or subatomic level. The boundary problem poses an obstacle to such theories of cons
field: Alternative archaeology / Vedic perspectives on consciousness
notable: Author of 'Forbidden Archeology' (1993, with Richard L. Thompson); member of ISKCON and Bhaktivedanta Institute
notes: Work is widely considered pseudoarchaeology by mainstream scholars. Vedic creationist. Also known as Drutakarma dasa. No formal academic appointment.
